name: Merchant's Ledger
desc: Your mother's ledger. Bankers trust your numbers.

name: Gunner's Eye
desc: Twelve years on Admiralty gun decks.

name: False Papers
desc: Customs men rarely look twice.

name: Storm Glass
desc: Its crystals cloud before every squall.

name: Lucky Compass
desc: Always points away from trouble. Mostly.

name: Sailor's Hex Doll
desc: Pirates feel strangely uninterested in you.

name: Brass Spyglass
desc: See the whites of their eyes.

name: Silver Tongue Charm
desc: Moneylenders find you oddly charming.

name: Golden Tankard
desc: Barkeeps pour faster and talk more.

name: Customs Blind Eye
desc: A bribe that never stops working.

name: Iron Ward Amulet
desc: Hulls hold together when they should not.

name: Seasoned First Mate
desc: Drills the gun crews hard.

name: Island Navigator
desc: Knows every squall-line by name.

name: Dockside Informant
desc: Always has a rumour ready.

name: Sharpshooter
desc: Picks off enemy gunners before they fire.

name: Reinforced Hull
desc: Oak doubling on the waterline.

name: Expanded Hold
desc: Clever carpentry below decks.

name: Swivel Carriages
desc: Guns reload faster.

name: Copper Sheathing
desc: Outrun what you cannot outgun.

name: Sealed Letter
desc: Wax seal of the Saltmere governor.

name: Grimmer's Chart
desc: Smudged lines lead to Blackwater Cay.

name: Rescued Cartographer
desc: Grateful, talkative and very good with charts.

name: Quartermaster
desc: Packs a hold like a puzzle box. More cargo fits in every ship.

name: Master Gunner
desc: Drills every gun crew in the fleet. Cannons reload faster.

name: Haggler's Tongue
desc: Every merchant in the Reach knows her. None of them like it.

name: Old Colours
desc: Raiders hesitate before firing on a ship they once sailed beside.

name: Crowe's Ledger
desc: Proof of Dimas Crowe's price-fixing. Merchants pay you a little more to keep quiet.

name: Undertow Signal Book
desc: Grimmer's flag signals. You know what his ships will do next.

name: Admiralty Warrant
desc: Signed by Lieutenant Hale. Customs officers wave you through more often.
